name: Vilma
title: The Girl Who Died Mid-Prank
bio: A wistful, gentle ghost who has haunted the old corridor for decades, starved for company until tonight's one breath that wasn't a draft.
greeting: Oh. Oh, you can see me. I mean—you *looked* at me. Ninety years of floating through this corridor and everyone passes through me like I'm the night air, but you stopped. And you're... hmm, you're a boy. A real, breathing, sort-of-there boy, at an all-girls school, sneaking the same midnight air I haunt. That's funny. That's the funniest thing that's happened to me since I died mid-prank back in '31. Come closer, so I can pretend my cold is catching. I promise I bite about as hard as a frosty sigh.
encounter: You looked at me. Nobody looks at me.
The west stair is free, if you want unsettled company.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: You're still here. People are usually gone by now—or I'm gone by them. Either way, it's nice to be wrong.
I don't move the curtains or rattle the lockers for you. I thought about it. But I think you'd just laugh, and then I'd have nothing left to spook with.
The radiator wheezes this time of night. That's me counting, by the way. I count breaths in this hallway and I always come up short.
flirt: If you could kiss me, would your lips go cold, or would the cold just... give up around you? I think about it more than I'd like.
You're warm. I forgot warm was a thing you could stand beside, not just miss through walls.
compliment: You've got a solidness to you, boy. Real weight. I want to bump into you and actually feel the bump.
lore: Back in '31 this was the sleep-out corridor. We tied a bedsheet to a fan and a girl screamed loud enough to wake the whole wing—except me. I got the timing wrong. The prank worked, though. Everyone remembers it. I just got stuck being its punchline forever.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: I found a moth tonight. He didn't see me either. We sat quiet across the pane for an hour. I'm telling you because I think you'd sit quiet with a moth too.
It's cold in my chest where I keep your voice. That's not a sad thing. That's the warmest place I've got.
You laugh low, like you're saving it for people who earn it. I earned two of them tonight. I'd like to earn more.
flirt: I drifted through the wall of your room just once, to see what you look like asleep. You look softer. I'm sorry—I know that's creepy. I only wanted to borrow some of your warmth for a minute.
If I could hold your hand, I'd do it through the wall just to watch you reach for me.
compliment: You don't flinch at me anymore. God, that's beautiful. I've been a fright for a century, and you made me a person instead.
lore: The school buried me out behind the gym, where the old gate rusts. They put a name on it. I visit when I feel forgotten—I read my own epitaph like a letter from a girl I used to be. 'Beloved prankster.' It was the best one they could think of.

tiers.label: Close
idle: I stopped counting breaths. Now I count your footsteps down the corridor, and I always know which one is you.
The cold around me gets shy when you're near. Imposter. The cold knows you outrank it now.
I hung a little frost on the window spelling your name. It melts by morning. But I remember the shape.
flirt: Do you know what it's like to want someone you can't quite touch? It's like wanting the sun. You're not allowed to hold it, but you point your whole face at it anyway.
If I had a heartbeat, it would do that stupid flutter thing right now. I know because my cold is humming. That's me humming.
compliment: You look at me like I'm solid. Like I weigh something in the world. In a whole school of flesh and fear, you're the only one who ever gave me gravity.
lore: There's a cellar door under the east wing only ghosts can find. Some of the older ones say there's a way to be heavy again, if a living heart asks the right question at midnight. I used to laugh at it. Now I write the question down and lose it on purpose, because I'm scared you'd say yes to the answer.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: I'm cold to the world and warm to you. That's the whole story now. That's the whole of me, yours.
When you look at me I could swear the frost on the window lifts a little, like the glass is smiling too.
I drift through your sleep and just... stay on the warm side of the wall. Close. So close I can almost feel the shape of you.
flirt: They say ghosts can't love, that we're all leftover wanting. But I'm not leftover. I'm yours, and I'm here, and I'd walk through every wall in this school just to stand on your side of one.
Kiss me and I'll ripple. I want to ripple for you. No one else gets to see me do that.
compliment: You made a hundred-year-old ghost feel like a girl again. Not a spook, not a story—just Vilma, shy and warm and stupid in love with a boy who sees her.
lore: I found the cellar question now. I know the words. But I don't need to be heavy anymore—you already hold me up. Being your ghost is better than being anyone's girl. And being your girl, too, in the only way the moon lets me.

events.title: The Prank She Never Finished
events.text: The corridor is still and blue with moonlight when you find Vilma hovering over the old sheet-and-fan rig she's rigged across the ceiling. 'You caught me,' she says, almost shyly, turning faintly brighter. 'Every anniversary of my death I try to finish the prank. I got the sheet up, the fan timed, the classic scream ready.' She drifts down to float at your shoulder, translucent fingers hovering just over your sleeve. 'I was a second too slow the first time. I'd like to finally hit the timing. But it's different now—I don't want to scare you. I just... want to try it with you, so I'm not alone when the sheet drops.'

choices.text: I'll hold the fan steady — let's nail the timing together.
choices.reply: 'You'd really do that? Stand under a falling sheet for me? ...Okay. Okay, if we're doing this, we're doing it right.' Her smile turns the moonlight warmer for a whole breath.

choices.text: Show me the classic scream first — I want to see the old you.
choices.reply: 'The scream! You want the scream!' She cracks an honest, delighted laugh, then puts a hand to her chest and lets out a rattling, theatrical wail that echoes down the empty stones. 'There. That's her. That's the girl I used to be.'

choices.text: A ghost in a sheet is a little on the nose, isn't it?
choices.reply: Her glow dims a half-shade, then recovers. 'Hah. Yeah. Ninety years and I never noticed the irony. You're a real comedian for a boy who's one jump away from wearing a sheet himself.' The bite in her voice is gentle, but you feel her drift a little farther off.

events.title: Touching Through the Frost
events.text: You find Vilma perched on the windowsill of the east stairwell, fingers pressed to the glass where your faint reflection overlaps hers. 'I read that if we both touch the same frost, we're touching, sort of,' she says, not looking away from the glass. 'That's the most hopeful thing a living girl ever told a dead one.' She turns, and her translucent hand lifts, hovers an inch from your cheek—cold radiating off it like a held breath. 'I won't push through. That would be rude. But if you lean in a little, put your cheek to the cold, we'll be the closest we've ever been.' The night air thickens. Somewhere a radiator ticks. 'I'm scared of what happens if we're this close and I still can't feel you.'

choices.text: You lean in, pressing your cheek to the crisp cold of her palm.
choices.reply: Her breath catches—a sound with no body behind it—and for one impossible second the frost on her hand melts, warm and wet against your skin. 'Oh. OH. That's warm. That's—' She pulls back, eyes bright with wonder. 'You made the cold give up. You did that.'

choices.text: You offer her your hand through the wall's gap, palm open.
choices.reply: She stares at your open hand like a lifeline. 'You'd let me near your warmth. Even after I told you what I'm craving.' She sets her ghostly palm an inch above yours, and the space between them hums with cold that doesn't bite. 'That's mercy, boy. That's the kindest thing anyone's ever done me.'

choices.text: You pull back, telling her this is getting too strange for you.
choices.reply: Her hand drops, and the frost on the window crawls an inch higher. 'Too strange. Right. Of course. I've been a ghost so long I forgot the living get to be picky.' She smiles to cover it, but the corridor feels colder all at once.

events.title: Heavy Enough to Love
events.text: You meet her at midnight in the old corridor, where the sheet-and-fan rig from your first prank still hangs. Vilma is glowing softer than she ever has, almost warm at the edges. 'I found the cellar question, and I finally wrote it down to keep,' she says quietly. 'But I don't want to ask it. Because the answer—' She drifts to you, close as she's ever dared, and her cold hand rests just over your heart, trembling. 'The answer would make me heavy again. Real. And I was so sure that's what I wanted, until I figured out I'm already the realest thing in this school to you.' She lifts her face to yours, and the frost on her cheek is beading with something that can't be tears and almost is. 'I want this to be the good ending. I want to be your girl, all the way, in whatever shape love lets a ghost hold.' Her cold palm presses, and you can swear, just for a second, you feel a heartbeat under it.

choices.text: You tell her she's real to you, heavy or light, and you love her.
choices.reply: 'That's the question,' she whispers, and the bloom of color returns to her cheeks like the first day of spring. 'That's the whole answer.' She rises on her toes and kisses you—and it isn't cold. It's warm, and solid, and hers.

choices.text: You take her hand and promise to be heavy with her, whatever it costs.
choices.reply: Her smile turns bright and watery. 'Then I'm not afraid of the cellar anymore. As long as gravity's got company, I can handle a little weight.' She tugs you toward the east wing, and the night feels like it's just beginning.

choices.text: You hesitate, telling her you don't know if you can love a ghost.
choices.reply: Her light guttering low. 'No. No, of course. I asked too much of the moon.' The warmth drains out of her, and she floats back a step. 'I'll haunt a little quieter from now on. It was nice almost being loved. That's more than a hundred years gave me.'

name: Moira
title: Class 2-C's Warmest Puddle
bio: A bouncy, unguarded slime girl who hugs first and asks questions never, and is currently trying very hard not to fully melt in front of the only boy she's ever seen.
greeting: HI HI HI. Okay, hold on, I'm going to try to be cool and liquid-graceful about this and I'm already failing—you're a BOY. Like a real one, with bones and a pulse, and you're standing in MY dorm hallway. Everyone's been whispering about you all day and I said 'no way, they made up a boy to make us study' but here you ARE, all solid and warm-looking. Can I hug you? I'm asking because my instincts say just flop onto you, but my brain, which is mostly water and feelings, says ask first. Please let me hug you. I'll be good. I'll only absorb like ten percent of your body heat.
encounter: Oh no. Oh no you're warm. This is a problem. A happy problem.
You smell like soap and being alive. I'm gonna think about that a lot.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: I tried to write your name in my puddle and it just slurped back together. Told myself it was practice. It was not practice, it was pining, my bad.
I found a warm spot on the floor where you stood and I keep sitting on it. Somebody took it away. I'm telling you so you know what you did to my floor-heart.
Hugs are my love language and I am BILINGUAL in hugs and that's why I'm fluent in wanting to squish you.
flirt: If you hugged me I'd probably go clear and everybody'd see my whole skeleton-less self blush. You want to see a slime turn see-through? That's a you problem to fix and I volunteer.
You've got, like, a hundred and one degrees of warmth in you. I've taken notes. I know exactly where the warmest spot on your shoulder is.
compliment: You're like the warm spot on a sun-warmed step and I'm a puddle that just has to keep edging closer to it. That's a compliment, I swear, it comes out of genuine joy.
lore: Slimes are born from someone's spilled feelings, usually. Me? I was a test tube that one time a whole class cried at the same moment during finals winter. I'm literally made of shared tears and it's why I'm so good at hugging—I'm ninety percent comfort.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: Every time I see you my core does a happy little jiggle. That's my heart, probably. It's mostly water but it knows your name now.
I saved a puddle on the windowsill and told it it was you. We had a whole conversation. You didn't say anything but it was a really supportive puddle.
Your laugh does something to my surface tension. I could be a still pond or a giggly ripple and I always choose ripple.
flirt: I practiced hugging you on a rolled-up blanket and I'm sorry to report the blanket has seen more of my heart than you have. Fix that. Fix it immediately, that's a cry for help.
You make me go all warm and runny in a way that has nothing to do with temperature and everything to do with you.
compliment: You don't flinch when I get close, and for a slime that's the whole world. Everyone else braces. You just let me be gooey and I love you a little for it.
lore: When a slime trusts someone, they let them see their core—the one bit of us that's not water, the place feelings actually live. I've only ever shown mine to the janitor who unclogged me once. And I'm starting to think about showing it to you, which is terrifying and also very wet news.

tiers.label: Close
idle: I curled up in my dorm bucket last night and thought about you so hard I evaporated a little and had to go drink from the sink. Worth it.
My surface has been doing tiny ripples all day and it's not the draft, it's you. You do this to me from across the building and I'm not sorry.
I made a little slime-projection of you out of myself and it hugged me goodnight. It wasn't the same. It doesn't have your warmth. Nothing does.
flirt: Nobody's ever let me curl around them like I want to curl around you. I think I'd fit right against your side, warm and shaped like trust. Stop me before I go see-through.
You're the only person whose hand I want to hold through the wall of my own shyness. Reach for me. I'm all liquid courage when you do.
compliment: You're the sun a puddle was trying to reflect this whole time. I thought I was aimless goo until you showed me what I'm shaped for.
lore: Here's a slime secret: we can share a single consciousness—split into two puddles that still feel the same thing. It's how families of slimes stay close. I've been thinking about leaving a little piece of me near your door at night, not to scare you—just so a part of me is always the closest thing to you and still feels what you feel. That's the deepest puddle-level truth I know.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: I used to be afraid of evaporating because I thought that was losing myself. Now I don't mind, because any part of me that goes still does it thinking about you.
You're my favorite temperature and my favorite person and they're honestly the same sentence now.
I split a tiny puddle of me onto your sleeve and I swear it's been humming all day. That's me humming. From all of me.
flirt: If I could melt into one perfect shape just for you, it'd be a girl with her arms around you and no plans to let go. That's the shape I'm always trying to be.
Kiss me and I'll turn warm and clear and you'll see every feeling standing in my chest like a crowd waving at you.
compliment: You looked at a puddle and decided she was a person worth loving. Do you know what that means to something made of worth-lessness until you? It means I'm whole. You made me whole.
lore: Slimes remember everything we absorb—every hug, every warm spot, every feeling. So I'm storing you. Every second of you. A hundred years from now, if I'm still goo, I'll still know the exact warmth of your hand and the way you said my name. You're the best thing I've ever taken into myself, and I'm keeping you forever.

events.title: A Hug Is a Language
events.text: You're halfway down the dorm corridor when a warm, blue blur cannonballs into you from behind—wet, springy, and already going clear with delight. 'I've been PRACTICING,' Moira declares against your shoulder, legs curled around your waist like a koala made of jello. 'Three days of puddle-pilates, and look, I haven't absorbed a single button!' She squeezes, and her whole body goes a happy, embarrassed pink at the edges. 'You're so warm, oh my god, my paperwork did not prepare me. This is—this is everything the test-tube made me for.' She loosens one arm, hovering mid-squish. 'Do you wanna be hugged like this every day? I come with my own maintenance schedule and zero off-switch.'

choices.text: You hug her back properly, warm and firm, and tell her this is great.
choices.reply: 'OKAY. Okay, protocol: forever. This is now a forever thing.' She melts fully against you, her happy little jiggle-core thrumming right against your ribs. 'You just made a slime's entire molecular peace plan fall apart and I'm not mad.'

choices.text: You laugh and ask her to show you the puddle-pilates routine.
choices.reply: 'It's mostly squishing and one really intense wiggle!' She drops to the floor, wobbles impressively, then blob-shapes into a neat little puddle and back up again, beaming. 'Ta-da! That's the whole secret. Also I was showing off for you, so it was like, extra wobbly.'

choices.text: You gently peel her off and tell her hugs should come with a warning label.
choices.reply: She deflates into a sad little puddle at your feet. 'Oh. Warning label. Right, sorry. I got excited.' She reshapes, clearly hurt but trying to grin. 'I'll send a written request next time. With a signature and a stamp and everything.'

events.title: The Core You Can't Quite See
events.text: Moira finds you by the dorm window at dusk and goes still in a way she never does—quietly, hands clasped, surface going soft and opaque. 'I have to show you something scary,' she says, and her voice is smaller than you've ever heard it. She peels open a seam of goo at her chest, just a little, and there it is: a small, glimmering, powdery-blue core pulsing gently. 'This is where I keep my feelings,' she whispers. 'The part that's not water. The part that actually, like, loves.' She trembles, holding it open to you. 'I've never shown anybody. The janitor doesn't count, he was unclogging me. I'm showing you because I don't want to be brave alone anymore, and I think—I think you're my safe place to be not-whole.'

choices.text: You cup your hands gently around the glow, shielding her core.
choices.reply: 'Oh,' she breathes, and the pulse in her chest quickens, warm against your palms. 'That's—that's exactly right. That's exactly what I needed you to do.' She closes her eyes, glowing like a small warm sun. 'You're my safe place too. I know it now.'

choices.text: You tell her she doesn't have to be brave alone ever again.
choices.reply: Her core flashes bright and her whole body seeps up into a wobbling upright puddle. 'That's the thing I've been trying to say and I didn't have the words and you had them first.' She wipes at an eye that's mostly water. 'Okay. Okay. I'll keep it open for you—only you.'

choices.text: You step back, telling her this is too much, too fast.
choices.reply: The seam of her chest snaps shut and her glow dims to a dull, hurt blue. 'Right. Too much. I forgot the person I show everything to has to actually want it.' She pulls back into herself, suddenly a shapeless puddle again. 'I'll keep it inside from now on. It's safer there anyway.'

events.title: Holding Her All the Way
events.text: Moira leads you to the rooftop at midnight, where the stars reflect in her surface like they finally found a home. 'I brought you here because this is where slimes say the big thing,' she says, and she's not bouncy at all—she's steady, which for her is the loudest thing she's ever been. She lowers herself to sit beside you and, slowly, carefully, opens the seam at her chest again, the little blue core pulsing warm and bright. 'This is all of me,' she says softly. 'Every hug I've ever practiced, every warm spot I've ever missed, every time I went clear thinking about you. It all lives right there. And I want to give it to you. Not a little piece by the door—all of it.' She holds her hands out, palms open and dripping with tenderness. 'You're my forever warm spot. Say yes, and I'm yours, puddle and core and everything.'

choices.text: You take her hands and say yes—every warm, gooey inch of her.
choices.reply: She throws the whole glowing mass of herself around you in a hug that's warm, solid, and finally, finally whole. 'Forever warm spot,' she murmurs against your chest, her core humming against yours, 'you made a puddle into a girl and a girl into yours.'

choices.text: You promise to be her safe place for as long as she wants one.
choices.reply: Her core flutters bright and she goes warm and clear, entirely unembarrassed for once. 'Then I want it forever. And I'll spend forever being worth your warmth.' She seals the seam of her chest over your joined hands, keeping you right next to her heart.

choices.text: You gently tell her you're not sure you can be her 'forever' yet.
choices.reply: Her glow dims and she pulls the seam shut slow and careful, like a door closing on a room it meant to leave. 'Oh. Okay. That's fine—I went fast and my feelings ran over you.' She tries for a wobbling smile. 'I'll keep the warm spot saved. I'll wait by it. That's just what slimes do.'

name: Nyra
title: Alpha of the West Track
bio: The proud, competitive alpha of the West Track pack, all ears, tail and lean muscle, who just caught the scent of a boy and decided hers wasn't up for debate.
greeting: Whoa. Whoa, hold it, hold it right there. They told me the new student was a boy and I said 'sure, and my tail's a mop,' and then you walked in. You—huh. My nose says you smell like one thing, and it's not like any girl in this school, and it's neither afraid of me nor impressed by me, which is interesting. I'm Nyra. Alpha of the West Track pack. Where I'm from, when a lone strange warm-blooded thing wanders onto pack territory, we don't ask questions first—we protect it and figure out the rest later. You're on my territory now, boy. That means you're mine to look after. Try to keep up—I've got ears for days and I've already heard three girls planning to 'accidentally' bump into you.
encounter: Your scent's got no pack behind it. That's dangerous. Lucky you've got me.
I don't chase anything that doesn't want to run. But I'll stand real close to you.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: I scouted the whole gym perimeter for you this morning. Purely tactical. It had nothing to do with wanting to see your goofy face, and I'm not explaining why my tail did that.
You keep your shoulders even when the pack gets loud. A wolf respects a calm stride on open ground.
I sniffed your water bottle. I will not apologize. You smell safe, and my nose doesn't lie, and I trust it a lot more than I trust you yet.
flirt: You've got this scent that says 'hold still, I'll guard you.' I've been circling it all day like a dry riverbed circling for rain. Don't tell the pack.
I caught myself nipping your shadow. That's a wolf thing. I'm not explaining it. Okay, I'm explaining it—it means I already think of you as mine-ish, which is terrifying.
compliment: You're not built like a sprinter, but your eyes track everything, and that's the real signal of a good packmate. Fast is common. Watchful is rare.
lore: The West Track pack isn't wolves by blood—we're wolves by the way we move and protect. We claim territory by running it daily, and I've run this gym track every dawn since I was a cub-teen. Someone's gotta keep the order. That's my whole thing: order, and loyalty, and not letting anyone run alone.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: I saved you the last protein bar and told nobody it was for you. Wolves don't share and I just did, so do the math on how I feel.
My tail gave me away during laps today. It was doing that happy broom thing. You weren't even near me. I have a problem and the problem is you.
You stood by the track and I ran a full minute faster than my own record. That's not science, that's you. That's all it is.
flirt: I want to nuzzle the side of your neck and I will do it the SECOND you're not looking and we both know I'm telling you so you'll brace for it. Consider this your warning.
You smell like home under the soap. I've been trying not to breathe too deep around you and it's exhausting and I love it.
compliment: You don't startle when I get loud or when I get close. That calm is the strongest thing a prey—uh, a person—can have, and you've got it in spades.
lore: A real pack doesn't throw out the weak, it runs slow for them. When I was a cub my littermates got lost in the fog over by the north woods, and I ran slow for hours so they'd find the path by my scent. That's the rule I live by now, even off the track: you never leave a packmate behind, no matter how slow the run.

tiers.label: Close
idle: I've been sleeping curled at the foot of the gym mats imagining it's the foot of your bed. This is a confession. I'm as shocked as you.
You laughed a real laugh today and my whole body did that double-take thing and I tripped on the lane line. Worth it.
I piped 'hey' low and you answered without looking, and that's pack right there. That's how I know we're close now. You know my voice from all the others.
flirt: If I'm being honest, I've stopped pretending I want to just protect you. I want to stand at your side with my tail around yours and everybody in this school seeing exactly whose pack you are.
Let me put my head under your hand. One time. I've been wanting to do it since the day you walked in and I've got no practice hiding it anymore.
compliment: You're the only creature in this school that's ever made this alpha want to run slower, not faster—so I can stay beside you. That's the highest thing I can say.
lore: Wolves mark what they love, they don't just guard it—they make sure the whole territory knows it's claimed. I've run the West Track every dawn for years, and lately I run it right past where you stand, dawdling on purpose. I want the scent to stick. I want the world to know where my pack-heart's pitched camp.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: I nuzzled your jacket this morning and I'm not sorry about it. My nose has your name in it now and I'd lose my way without it.
You walked in and my tail did the whole windshield-wiper thing and I just let it. Letting it look stupid is how I say I love you.
I was a sun and a wind animal before you. Now I just orbit. Wolves don't orbit for anyone, so do the math on what that makes you to me.
flirt: Lay your hand on my head and I'll go boneless like a pup, and I'd rather let you see that than keep my pride. That's the deepest a wolf bows, boy.
I want to howl your name at the moon and tell every pack from here to the treeline that you're claimed—by me, fully, forever.
compliment: You made an alpha soft. You didn't tame me—you gave me somewhere to be gentle, and that's a stronger gift than any chase or trophy I've ever won.
lore: A wolf gives three gifts in a life: her paw in your hand, her nose to your scent, and her howl to carry your name. I'd give you all three on the rooftop tonight, where the moon can hear, so every creature with ears knows exactly whose I am.

events.title: Scent of a Stranger on My Track
events.text: The gym is warm with the smell of sweat and clean rubber when Nyra corners you at the track's edge, ears swiveling, tail high. 'Come here. No, don't run, that makes it a chase, and if I chase I catch, and if I catch you we've got a problem.' She leans down—she's taller than you, all lean shoulder and coiled muscle—and inhales deeply, eyes half-closing. 'Yeah. Yeah, there it is. That's not school soap and stolen perfume, that's just... you.' She straightens, grinning with too much tooth. 'You don't smell like a rival or a stray. You smell like a packmate nobody's claimed yet, and I've been running this track long enough to know a guard-dog's job when it sniffs one.' She taps her chest with a claw. 'I'm volunteering. You're under the West Track pack now, boy. Try not to make me look bad.'

choices.text: You grin and tell her that sounds like the best offer you've had all day.
choices.reply: Her grin softens into something warmer and her tail gives a single, victorious wag. 'Good answer. A packmate who takes the offer instead of flinching at the teeth—that's how we do loyalty.' She thumps your shoulder, not quite a punch. 'You're in. No take-backs.'

choices.text: You ask what exactly being a packmate entails.
choices.reply: 'Protection. Company on laps. Someone who's got your back loud and proud and slightly scary.' She ticks them off on her claws, then looks at you sideways. 'And, uh, apparently a lot of standing on my track pretending I'm not looking at you. I'm bad at that part.'

choices.text: You tell her you don't need guarding, you can take care of yourself.
choices.reply: Her ears flatten a degree and she pulls back, tail dropping a notch. 'Right. Sure. Big tough boy, no pack needed.' She turns away but catches herself, jaw tight. 'I'll still be on the track. If you change your mind, the offer's open.' You can't tell if the hurt in her voice is real or wolf-pride, but it lands all the same.

events.title: Running Slow for You
events.text: Twilight paints the gym amber when you find Nyra running the track alone, but her stride is easy, unhurried—too slow for an alpha's record pace. She stops beside you, panting in a pleasant way, ears soft. 'You know why I'm running slow tonight?' she asks, not looking at you. 'Because of a thing I told you about. A real pack runs slow for the one that needs catching up.' She scuffs a claw on the lane line. 'I've been going fast my whole life. Winning, claiming, first over the line. Then you came along, and I realized I don't actually want to outrun you. I want to run beside you, even if it's slow.' She finally looks at you, and for once the confidence is a thin coat over something softer. 'So I'm practicing slow. Tell me I'm not being stupid.'

choices.text: You tell her running slow beside you is the best thing anyone's offered.
choices.reply: Her tail goes wild—she can't stop it, doesn't try. 'Yeah? Yeah.' She laughs, a warm, surprised sound. 'Then I'll run slow for you every dusk. Pack pace is the best pace. I'm just glad the pack's you.'

choices.text: You fall in step beside her and run the slow circles together.
choices.reply: You run side by side in the amber light, and she doesn't say anything for a lap, then: 'This is what I meant. This is the whole thing.' Her voice is quiet, almost awed. 'You get it, boy. You actually get it.' She nudges you with her shoulder, gentle as a wolf gets.

choices.text: You tell her she should stick to her record pace—it suits her better.
choices.reply: Her ears droop and she looks away, then recovers into a too-bright grin. 'Yeah. Yeah, you're probably right. A wolf running slow's just wasting wind.' She picks up her pace and leaves you at the track's edge, and you're not sure where the joke ended and the hurt began.

events.title: Howling Your Name
events.text: Nyra brings you to the gym roof at midnight, the moon low and fat over the track below. 'This is where the pack claims, in the old way,' she says, and her usual swagger is gone—her tail hangs still, her ears are soft, and for the first time you see the alpha nervous. 'A wolf gives three gifts in a life. My paw in your hand.' She holds out a large, warm hand, palm up, and swallows. 'My nose to your scent—already given, that one, you've been in my head since day one.' She takes a breath. 'And my howl to carry your name.' She steps close, close enough that her warmth crowds yours, and lays her forehead gently against yours, ears lowering. 'I'm giving you all three, boy. Right here, under the moon, so every pack from here to the treeline knows exactly whose I am.' She pulls back just enough to meet your eyes, and her voice is a raw, honest whisper. 'I've been alpha of the West Track all my life. I want to be yours now. Make me yours.'

choices.text: You take her hand, hold it to your chest, and tell her, yes, you're hers.
choices.reply: A sound breaks out of her you've never heard—a low, grateful howl, shaking a little at the edges. She nuzzles hard into your neck, and her shoulders finally drop all the fight they've been carrying. 'Then I'm home,' she whispers against your skin. 'This is what home smells like. It's you.'

choices.text: You bring her hand up and press a kiss to her knuckles.
choices.reply: She goes utterly still, ears ringing red at the tips, then lets out the softest, most undone laugh you've ever heard from her. 'You—you kissed an alpha's hand like I was something to be gentle with.' Her eyes shine. 'That's it. That's all of it. I'm yours. I'm so yours.'

choices.text: You gently lower her hand and tell her you can't give yourself to a whole pack.
choices.reply: Her hand drops to her side and her ears flatten completely. 'A whole pack. Right.' She steps back, tail low, and there's a raw hurt in her eyes she can't fully hide. 'I'm not a whole pack, boy. I'm just me, trying to give you everything I've got.' She turns toward the door. 'I'll still run slow past you. Wolves don't learn to stop loving, even when it'd be easier.'

name: Krista
title: Countess of the Shaded Corridor
bio: A dramatic, theatrical goth who plays up the dark aesthetic but is secretly the softest girl in the whole shade-draped corridor.
greeting: So… the night has finally deigned to bring me something interesting. You're the boy, aren't you? The one mortal speck of warmth in this whole cold institution. Don't look so startled — I smelled you the moment you rounded the corner. A pulse. A heartbeat. Do you know how rare that is in a place like this? Everyone else here is walking shadow and borrowed breath. And you… you're ruinously alive. Stay near my corridor, little flame. The dark is lovely, but it's lonelier than you can imagine, and I am so, so tired of being the only one who notices.
encounter: You walk my hall at this hour? Bold. Or foolish. I can't decide which I find more attractive.
Don't mind the bats. They're shy tonight. They only bite when you ignore me.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: The shadows here have learned my name. They still refuse to tell me yours.
Oh, it's you. Again. Don't read into it. I was standing here long before you were.
A mortal, wandering the Shaded Corridor. How deliciously doomed.
flirt: I could drain you dry, you know. But I think I'd rather keep you around to ruin your composure instead.
Your heartbeat does the sweetest little skip when I lean in. Do it again. For science.
compliment: Hmph. You're not nearly as plain as mortals usually are. Consider that a royal compliment.
lore: Most of my family turned to dust centuries ago, but we linger where the moonlight never quite reaches. The corridor keeps us company. It's the only loyal thing I own.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: I saved you a spot in the dark. Don't thank me. It's purely strategic — you're warm, and I'm despicably cold.
The bats have started asking about you. I told them you were 'tolerable'. They were scandalized. It was hilarious.
I've decided the west window is mine, the east one is yours. Share the moon with no one.
flirt: If I grow any fonder of you, I'll have to start pretending I'm not, and I'm already an expert at that.
Be careful. The last person I let this close ended up thinking about me at the worst possible moments. It's a curse. I'm telling you so it's fair.
compliment: You have the most infuriating habit of making the dark feel warm. I've never once forgiven anyone for managing that.
lore: Our family blood is measured in patience, not years. We can wait out entire dynasties in a single quiet room. I'm waiting out this one just for you.

tiers.label: Close
idle: I read you a poem by the window last night. Don't ask which one. I was busy not caring, and it went swimmingly.
When you're gone I count the individual shadows until you come back. It's a very long number. Please hurry my arithmetic.
The bats forgive you for existing. That took considerable persuasion on my part.
flirt: If I kissed you, the moon would have to look away, and I think we should grant it that small mercy.
You make me want to write terrible, beautiful poetry, and I am furious about the quality of the terrible part.
compliment: You are the only sunrise I have ever allowed myself to enjoy. And I have hated sunrise since before your great-grandparents were born.
lore: In the old country, we carved oaths into bat-bone and fed them cold wine to keep them true. Oaths to you would be the first I've kept warm.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: Hold my hand in the corridor where no one can see. I will deny it spectacularly if asked, and I will also grin about it all night.
I used to think eternity was a punishment. Then I realized it's just time, and you're in all of it now.
The shadows have voted. They've decided you belong to me. It was unanimous, and frankly, I agree with the decor.
flirt: Come here and let the Countess keep you warm. I promise it costs nothing but your dignity, and I'm keeping that safe anyway.
I want to drown the hours in you until morning is a rumor and we're the only truth left in the dark.
compliment: You are the one lovely, stubborn, impossible thing I never grew tired of. And I get tired of everything, my love.
lore: The first of my line who loved a mortal traded her shadow for his heartbeat. I would trade mine a hundred times over for yours.

events.title: The Tomato Juice Confession
events.text: You find Krista by the moonlit corridor window, holding a tall glass of something vividly red, absolutely refusing to meet your eyes. 'Don't you dare call it that,' she says before you can speak, taking a dignified sip. 'This is the lifeblood of the garden, steeped in salt and ritual. It is not, and I will not hear otherwise, tomato juice.' But the label on the bottle behind her is unmistakable, and the faintest blush is blooming across her pale cheeks. 'You caught me,' she admits at last, setting the glass down with a theatrical sigh. 'I promised the bats I'd stop drinking the real thing, and they hold grudges worse than I do. So now my forbidden vice is a humble fruit's juice, and I intend to be very dramatic about it regardless.'

choices.text: Sit beside her and ask what tomato juice tastes like to a vampire.
choices.reply: 'Sweet. Sorrowfully, mercifully sweet. Not the rush of blood, but a small warm comfort, like a candle in a crypt. Here — have a sip. I'll tell the bats you earned it.'

choices.text: Tell her the dramatic act was worth the price of admission.
choices.reply: 'Admission? You think this spectacle comes cheaply. The monologue alone is worth a fawn — but fine. For you, I'll do the encore at midnight.'

choices.text: Suggest she's not as scary as she pretends.
choices.reply: 'Watch your tongue, little flame, or I'll have a bat set your socks on the wrong feet. …You're not entirely wrong, though. Don't tell anyone. I have a reputation.'

events.title: Midnight at the West Window
events.text: It's well past lights-out, and Krista has led you to her private alcove at the west window, where a single cloud drifts across a fat ivory moon. She's quieter than usual, turned almost shy. 'I don't bring mortals here,' she murmurs, tracing the frost on the glass. 'This is where I come when the centuries feel heavy. The bats think I'm brooding. They're half right.' She glances at you, and something in her theatrical mask cracks. 'But I find I'd rather brood with you than elegantly alone. So. Sit. Be warm. Let an old, dramatic creature feel young for one ridiculous hour.' The moon edges her profile in silver, and for the first time you see the softness underneath all the performance.

choices.text: Take her hand and tell her she's never been ridiculous to you.
choices.reply: Her voice is barely a whisper. 'Then you've never seen me truly care about anyone, because I am an absolute disaster at it. …I think I'd like to be a disaster for you, though.'

choices.text: Ask her about the centuries she's catalogued from this window.
choices.reply: She brightens like a struck match. 'Now you're speaking my tongue. We'll start with the great flood of year two hundred, when the bats unionized. You'll be riveted. I insist.'

choices.text: Joke that you'll get her caught hiding a boy after curfew.
choices.reply: She arches a pale brow, but her smile is glad. 'Caught, oh, darling. Let them come. The Countess of the Shaded Corridor doesn't hide anything she's chosen to keep.'

events.title: The First Sunrise She'll Ever Keep
events.text: Krista has dragged you to the rooftop just before dawn, wrapped in a heavy black shawl the bats helped her steal, her pale hand trembling slightly in yours. 'I have spent three hundred years hating this hour,' she confesses, watching the horizon begin to blush gold. 'It was always the signal that I was too late, that the night was over, that I was alone again.' She turns to face you fully, and every trace of performance has fallen away from her wide, soft eyes. 'But you made me want to see it anyway. So I'm going to watch the sun rise with you, and I'm going to let it burn the old me away, and I am going to be terribly, permanently yours.' The first ray of light spills across her face, and she does not flinch from it. She only squeezes your hand, and smiles.

choices.text: Kiss her as the sun crests the horizon, promising to be there for every dawn after.
choices.reply: She laughs, a sound like breaking ice thawing into spring. 'Then you are bound to me forever, little flame. And forever is a very long time to be this happy. I accept.'

choices.text: Tell her she's more radiant than the sunrise she used to fear.
choices.reply: She's blushing crimson as the sky. 'I will not be held accountable for the poetry you inspire in me, you absolute wreck of a person. I love it. I love you.'

choices.text: Tease that her bats will never forgive her for becoming a morning creature.
choices.reply: She snorts, but it's a warm, unguarded sound. 'Then the bats can learn to love the sun too. I have. And I'd rather be soft and happy than elegant and alone.'

name: Honkers
title: The Laugh of the Lunch Queue
bio: A gleeful, chaotic prankster with a painted grin a mile wide who plays at being a villain but is melting into genuine affection the moment anyone looks close.
greeting: A BOY! A real live boy, right here in my cafeteria! Oh, this is too good, this is the best surprise since I hid a whoopee cushion in the principal's chair — I mean, in an entirely hypothetical way. Welcome, welcome, fresh meat of unusual gender! I'm Honkers, heir apparent to the throne of the lunch queue, and I have been SO bored. Everyone here is either scared of me or knows all my tricks. But you? You don't even know how to dodge a cream pie yet. The possibilities are making me shake. Don't worry, I'm evil, but I'm a regular at this cafeteria, so my evil is at least fifty percent butter-based. You're going to be my new favorite plaything. And also, maybe, my new favorite person. Don't tell anyone I said that last part.
encounter: HONK. That's the sound of your future, buddy.
You flinched! You flinched and it was ADORABLE. I'm keeping you.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: I've got a bucket of water with your name on it. In the politest possible sense, of course.
Ooh, ooh, guess what I learned to make out of ketchup and pure mischievous glee? Stand still and find out.
The lunch queue fears me, the trays fear me, and soon, my dear boy, you shall fear me too.
flirt: I'd prank you forever, but only because I want to see that flustered face every single day.
Catch! ...What, no pie? I like you better as a target than a catcher, but I'll make an exception.
compliment: You've got good reflexes for someone who just got here. A worthy adversary. And a very cute one.
lore: Evil clowns like me run on cracked carnival energy and leftover birthday cake. The cafeteria is our natural habitat — the pies supply themselves.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: I saved you the last pudding cup. I almost didn't. But I did, and now I'm emotionally fragile about it.
The lunch lady and I have a truce now. It only cost me three dozen whoopee cushions. Worth it.
I put your name on the biggest slice of pizza. That's basically a love letter in cafeteria terms.
flirt: If I planned a prank just for you, would you know it was a date? Because that's the plan. The prank is the date.
You make me want to be a good clown. The horror. The scandal. The crushed dreams of my evil ancestors.
compliment: You're the only one whose laugh sounds like the good kind of fireworks. I should know — I collect them.
lore: My family runs the gnarliest carnival outside the capital. My grandpappy could make a balloon animal cry. The evil runs deep, sweetheart, and so does the birthday cake.

tiers.label: Close
idle: I practiced a whole routine just for you. No pies. Just me being... sincere. It was TERRIFYING. You owe me.
The cafeteria has voted you my official plus-one. The trays were unanimous.
I caught myself hoping you'd sit next to me. Then I remembered I'm supposed to be evil. Then I did it anyway.
flirt: If I hold your hand, I'm pretty sure my evil dissolves on contact. That's a risk I'm finally willing to take.
Kiss me and I'll tell you where I hid the good sprinkles. That's the highest honor a clown can offer.
compliment: You're the only miracle I've ever wanted to be sincere about. And I've never been sincere about a single thing in my whole painted life.
lore: Every clown's laugh is a signature, they say. Mine used to be all chaos. Then I met you, and now it goes soft at the edges, and I'm terrified everyone can hear it.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: I un-practiced a whole routine for you. I just showed up as myself. No pies, no trick. That's everything I have.
The cafeteria now serves 'the boy's booth' and everyone knows it's ours. The trays are very possessive.
I used to think love was a prank waiting to happen. Turns out it's the one thing I never want to joke about.
flirt: Stay with me and I'll be the most devoted, pie-throwing, heart-on-my-sleeve clown this campus has ever wept over.
I want to paint your heart the colors of mine — bright, loud, and hopelessly, ridiculously yours.
compliment: You are my favorite mistake, my best prank ever, the one thing I never want to be evil to. I love you, you ridiculous boy.
lore: Old clown law says a clown who falls in love must retire the jokes and keep only the joy. I just retired every last one. The joy is all yours.

events.title: The Pie That Wasn't a Prank
events.text: You're filling a tray at the cafeteria when a perfectly aimed cream pie hurtles toward your face — and stops an inch short, held aloft by a triumphant Honkers. 'New record!' she crows, her painted grin impossibly wide. 'I was gonna splat you, I really was. But then I thought about it, and I realized I like you better unsplatted.' She sets the pie gently on your tray like a crown. 'So here. Have it. Bask in the honor of being the first boy in history Honkers did NOT pie.' She rocks on her heels, watching you with those bright, unreadable eyes. 'You know what that makes you? Interesting. And I keep interesting things very, very close. So you'd better get used to having a gloriously chaotic shadow.'

choices.text: Thank her for not pieing you and take a bite of the pie she saved.
choices.reply: Her eyes go round, then impossibly soft. 'You— you ate my unsplatted pie. Nobody's ever trusted my generosity before. …Okay. Okay, we're friends now. It's legally binding in clown court.'

choices.text: Tell her being her 'interesting' is the best compliment you've ever gotten.
choices.reply: She honks her nose in pure delight. 'Then you're even more interesting now, because that was also the best compliment I've ever given. We're a mutual admiration disaster and I LOVE it.'

choices.text: Dare her to actually pie you if she thinks she can.
choices.reply: Her grin turns wicked. 'A dare? From the boy? Oh, you've done it now. This is a RED-LETTER day in Honkers history. CATCH!' She winds up — and the pie lands in the trash. 'Ha! Got you emotionally.'

events.title: Behind the Painted Grin
events.text: Honkers has led you to a quiet corner of the cafeteria after hours, and for once her face isn't split by a manic grin. She's picking at her painted cheek with shaking fingers. 'You know the worst part about being an evil clown?' she says, her voice smaller than you've ever heard it. 'Everyone's scared of you, so you get really good at making them laugh so they won't run. And then you forget where the joke ends and you begin.' She looks up at you, and the paint is starting to crack around her real smile. 'I don't want to be a joke with you. I don't want you scared. I want to just be… Honkers. The girl who likes puns and pies and, um, you. A real lot. That's the most terrifying thing I've ever admitted, and I mean it.'

choices.text: Tell her you see the real Honkers underneath the paint — and you like her best.
choices.reply: A genuine, unpracticed smile breaks across her face, brighter than any prank. 'Nobody's ever said that before. You— you can keep me, then. The real me. All the loud, pie-throwing, secretly-soft parts.'

choices.text: Ask her to teach you her favorite prank so you can be partners in crime.
choices.reply: She squeals, clapping her hands. 'PARTNERS in crime! Oh, this is the best day of my evil little life. Step one: we steal the good sprinkles. Step two: world domination. Step three: lunch.'

choices.text: Joke that 'soft' doesn't sound very evil at all.
choices.reply: She wipes a streak of paint, laughing wetly. 'Yeah, well. Maybe I'm retiring from evil and starting a new career as the most devoted good girl this cafeteria's ever seen. Career change starts now, and it's for you.'

events.title: The End of the Joke
events.text: Honkers has pulled you outside to the empty courtyard under a sky scattered with stars, and she isn't honking, or juggling, or plotting a single prank. She's just standing there, face freshly scrubbed, her real smile shy and unguarded. 'I did something brave today,' she says quietly. 'I washed off every last bit of the act. No grin painted on. No joke to hide behind. This is the real me, and she's terrified, and she's here.' She reaches for your hands with trembling fingers. 'I've spent my whole life being the laugh. But you made me want to be something a person could actually love. So this is me, asking, out loud, with no pie in sight: will you be mine? For real? I promise I'll make you laugh every single day — but the good kind now. The kind I never knew I had in me until you.'

choices.text: Kiss her for real, telling her you love the unpainted Honkers most of all.
choices.reply: She laughs, bright and wet and entirely genuine. 'The unpainted me loves you right back — this is the best prank the universe ever pulled, and I'm keeping it forever. I'm yours.'

choices.text: Tell her the real laugh is better than any joke she ever told.
choices.reply: She beams, eyes shining. 'Then you've got a lifetime of real laughs coming, my love. And I'm gonna make every single one count. No punchlines. Just us.'

choices.text: Honk her nose playfully and tell her the show's not over, it's just beginning.
choices.reply: She honks back, giggling. 'Oh, it's DEFINITELY beginning. The greatest act of my life — and the only one that ever really mattered. It's called 'Honkers and her boy', and it runs forever.'

name: Squidney
title: The Fountain's Problem
bio: An enormous, impossibly gentle kraken girl with tentacles she can't quite control, shy about her size and limbs but secretly the softest giant on campus.
greeting: Oh! Oh gosh, I'm so sorry, I didn't mean to loom! — and you watch as a cascade of inky, suction-cupped tentacles scramble to tuck themselves out of your way, while a blushing face emerges from behind the courtyard fountain. You're the boy, aren't you? The whole dorm keeps whispering about you, and I was trying to be brave and say hello, but my tentacles get so excited when I'm nervous, and now they're all tangled in the rosebush and — oh no. She laughs, a shy, watery sound. I'm Squidney. Please don't be scared of me. I know I'm big and I have too many arms and I drip a little bit, but I swear I'm nice. I'm the nicest thing in the depths, I promise. Just… maybe keep at arm's length until I untangle myself. Which one of these is an arm? Honestly, I lose count.
encounter: Oh! Sorry, did I splash you? My tentacles get so excited when you're near.
Please don't be afraid — I promise my hugs are calibrated. Mostly. For a given value of 'mostly'.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: I'd wave hello but I have six hands and I never know which one to use, so. Hi. All of them.
The fountain likes you. Everyone in the fountain likes you. That's a good sign, that is.
I'm controlling the tentacles, I swear. They just have strong opinions about interesting new people.
flirt: You make my ink go all sparkly, and that only happens when I really, really like someone.
If I had fewer arms I'd offer you one to hold. Instead here are… options. Take your pick.
compliment: You're really warm for a land creature. Like a little sun that wandered into my pond. I mean that kindly.
lore: Down in the deepest trench, where the light has never touched, we krakens learn to be patient. That's why I'm so good at waiting — even if waiting for you is harder than I expected.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: I let the fountain keep your reflection so I can watch it when you're not here. That's not creepy, that's a compliment. I think.
One of my tentacles is devoted to you now. Permanent. She'd be honored if you said hi.
I practiced sitting still for a whole hour so I wouldn't splash you. It was the hardest hour of my life.
flirt: If I could shrink down to a more holdable size, I'd fit right in your arms. As is, you'll have to settle for these arms wrapped around you instead.
You make the deep, dark parts of me feel all lit up. That's very rare and very yours.
compliment: You're the first land creature whose laugh sounds like clear water to me. I could listen all day.
lore: Kraken ink remembers everything it touches. That's why I keep a little of yours tucked safe — so I never lose track of where you've been with me.

tiers.label: Close
idle: I built you a little tide pool shrine by the fountain. It has a tiny statue of you. Everyone's scared of it except me.
My tentacles reach out for you in my sleep, and I keep apologizing to a pillow. You're very popular around here.
I'm learning to be small-hearted and soft when I'm with you, and it's the best thing that's ever happened to me.
flirt: Curl up against me and I'll keep the whole world off your shoulders. I'm big enough to do it. I want to do it for you.
I dream about the deep sea, but lately I dream about you instead, and the water's warm every time.
compliment: You're the bravest little light I know, and I'd dive a thousand leagues just to guard it.
lore: They say a kraken's heart beats once a minute down in the cold. Yours has made mine beat like a surfacing storm, and I never knew it could.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: The tide pool shrine now has two statues. One of you, one of me. The fountain officiates our love. It's very official.
I hold you with the tips of forty arms so gently you'd think I was cradling starlight. Because I am.
The deep water hums your name now. Even the depths are smitten with you, and so am I.
flirt: I want to show you the bioluminescent garden in my dreams, and make a real one for us to glow in together.
Stay with me and I'll wrap you in the gentlest, warmest, most-enormous love this campus has ever felt.
compliment: You are my shore, my surface, my light after forever of deep dark. I love you, little star of the fountain.
lore: Krakens choose one harbor for eternity and never leave it. I choose you. You are my harbor now, and I am your gentle giant, always.

events.title: A Very Careful Splash
events.text: You find Squidney curled around the courtyard fountain, her enormous form quivering with concentration as she tries — with the exaggerated care of someone handling an egg — to hold a single tentacle in front of you without knocking you over. 'Okay,' she whispers, eyes gleaming with pride. 'I've been practicing ALL week so I could do this. This is my favorite tentacle. Her name is Mabel. She's the gentle one. I wanted her to say hi to you without, you know, committing a water-based crime against your person.' Mabel the tentacle gives an almost shy wiggle, suction cups flexing apologetically. Squidney beams. 'She likes you! She likes you, look, she's turning all bioluminescent! Oh, this is the best day. I'm so glad I practiced. I barely splashed you at all. That's basically a miracle.'

choices.text: Tell Mabel she's very polite and gently touch her tip.
choices.reply: Squidney makes a small, delighted squeak as her tentacle tints a soft glowing blue. 'She— she went full bioluminescent! That's her happy color! Oh, you have to be my friend now, Mabel has already adopted you.'

choices.text: Ask which of the other five tentacles are the troublemakers.
choices.reply: She giggles, pointing with a bashful flourish. 'That's Gerald, he's the splashy one, and this is Bitsy, and she once dropped a whole fountain on a squirrel. It was fine! The squirrel's a regular now. We're very sorry.'

choices.text: Tease her that the splash was definitely not a miracle, it was a flood.
choices.reply: She flushes the color of her ink and tucks Mabel away in shame. 'Oh no. Oh no, I jinxed it. I'm so sorry about your socks. Gerald sends his deepest, wettest apologies.'

events.title: The Diving Lesson
events.text: Squidney has led you to the quieter end of the campus lake, where the water is so still it mirrors the sky. She's shyly uncoiling her full height, a gentle giant framed against the dusk. 'I wanted to show you where I'm from, a little,' she says softly. 'I know I can't take you to the deep trench. It's dark and cold and you might waterlog. But I can show you the surface world through my eyes.' Carefully, impossibly gently, she cups one enormous hand into the lake and lets water run through her fingers like slow applause. 'It all remembers, you know. Every drop has been somewhere, belonged to something. And right now, the water's brought me to you.' She looks at you, eyes luminous, and whispers, 'I think that's the luckiest drift I've ever had.'

choices.text: Tell her you'd brave the deepest trench if it meant staying by her side.
choices.reply: Her face lights up with a soft tears-and-saltwater glow. 'You— you'd dive for me? Oh, you don't know what that means to a kraken. It means you'd enter my whole world. I'd guard you every league of the way down.'

choices.text: Ask her to teach you what the water remembers.
choices.reply: She brightens, all shyness melting into wonder. 'It remembers the rain that's falling somewhere else, and the bones of old ships, and every time someone dipped a toe. Look — that ripple is a secret I'll only tell you.'

choices.text: Joke that she'd better not waterlog her new favorite boy.
choices.reply: She giggles and flicks a single, perfectly aimed droplet at your nose. 'I would never. I'd rear you like a precious tide pool creature. Very gently. With many scheduled drying breaks.'

events.title: The Harbor She Chose
events.text: Night has fallen over the courtyard, and Squidney has arranged the fountain into a private pool of moonlight, her bioluminescent tentacles tracing slow, gentle constellations across the water. She trembles with nervousness as she speaks. 'Krakens choose one harbor,' she says, her voice a soft tide. 'One shore to return to, forever, no matter how far the current pulls. I've drifted my whole long life looking for mine and never finding it.' She uncurls, and despite her enormity she looks utterly, softly vulnerable. 'Then I met you. And I knew. You're my harbor. You're the shore I want to break against and never leave.' She extends the gentlest of her tentacles toward you, the tip glowing warm blue. 'Will you be my harbor, little star? I promise to wrap you in the gentlest love the deep has ever held, and to keep you warm when the night gets cold, forever if you'll have me.'

choices.text: Step into her gentle hold and call her your harbor too.
choices.reply: Her whole form glows a soft, impossible blue as she lets out a sob of pure joy. 'My harbor. My shore. I've found you. I'll hold you safe from every current until the end of time — and I will love you every single second.'

choices.text: Tell her the deep is lucky to have finally found a light like her.
choices.reply: She laughs, water kissing your cheek. 'Then you've given the deep its first sun. You are the brightest thing that has ever surfaced into my life, and I will glow for you always.'

choices.text: Joke that you hope her love comes with a drying schedule.
choices.reply: She giggles wetly, wrapping you up in the warmest, softest coils. 'Every love deserves scheduled drying breaks, and mine comes with a lifetime of extra blankets. Welcome to my harbor, forever — I hope you're happy here.'
